sections.heading: FDI vs FII/FPI — the definitional core

rows: Definition
Investment with **lasting interest & control** — ≥10% equity (IMF norm); greenfield plants, M&A, reinvested earnings
Financial-asset purchases **without control** — listed equity (<10%), bonds; SEBI-registered
Character
**Patient**: brings technology, management, market access, jobs; hard to exit (plant ≠ portfolio)
**Mobile**: deepens markets, funds the CAD cheaply; can exit in a day ('hot money')
Scale (India)
Gross ~**$70-85 bn/yr band** (net lower as repatriation rose); cumulative ~$1 trillion since 2000
Swings between +$40 bn and −$20 bn years — the volatility signature; bond-index era adds stable debt FPI
Regulation

FEMA + sectoral caps: **automatic route dominant**; prohibited (lottery, chit funds); capped-approval pockets (defence beyond 74%, insurance 100% (2025 move), multi-brand retail 51%-conditional); **Press Note 3 (2020)** — land-border-country approvals (the China screen)
SEBI FPI regulations; NRI-adjacent routes; **participatory notes** curbed for opacity

items: **FDI's benefits ledger**: non-debt financing of the CAD, technology-productivity spillovers (auto clusters' vendor deepening — **Kia's AP ecosystem the local proof**), export platforms (mobile phones' ~$25+ bn exports), competition-consumer gains, jobs; **costs ledger**: profit repatriation (the rising outflow line), crowding-out of domestic incumbents, tax games (transfer pricing; the treaty-shopping history Mauritius-Singapore fixed 2016), strategic-sector anxieties (PN3's logic), and 'brownfield ≠ new capacity' (M&A-heavy years add ownership change, not plants).

**FPI's benefits**: market depth-liquidity, cost-of-capital reduction, discipline signal; **costs**: sudden-stop risk (2008, 2013 taper, 2022 episodes — ₹ and reserves absorbing), volatility spillovers to rates-currency, governance short-termism; the **hierarchy verdict**: FDI > equity FPI > debt FPI > ECB in desirability — durable, risk-sharing capital first.

**Policy stance evolution**: 1991's opening → composite caps (2013) → automatic-route generalisation → **screening era (PN3 2020; global FDI-security trend)** — India courts capital while gating adversarial capital: the two-hands description.

**AP file**: Kia (~$2 bn+), Foxconn-era electronics at Sri City-Tirupati, greenfield ports' project FDI, aqua-processing JVs — the state competes on land-speed-coast (IDA-043's triad); FPI touches AP indirectly via listed financiers of its projects.

sections.heading: Monetary and fiscal policy — the two engines

rows: Objective
**Price stability (CPI 4±2%) while supporting growth** — the statutory mandate (2016)
Growth, distribution, stabilisation — the budget's triple function (Musgrave)
Instruments

**Repo rate** (the price of money), stance; **LAF corridor (SDF-MSF)**, OMOs & twists, **CRR (4-4.5% band)-SLR (18%)**, forex ops; regulation & macroprudential (risk weights — the 2023 unsecured-credit action)
Taxes-expenditure-borrowing mix; capex composition; deficits (GBI-018); counter-cyclical stance (COVID's ~9% deficit)
Transmission
Repo → bank MCLR/**EBLR (external benchmarks, 2019 — transmission's fix)** → credit-deposit rates → demand; lags 2-4 quarters
Multipliers: capex ~2.5-4x > revenue ~<1; immediate demand injection
Limits
Blunt against supply-shock inflation (vegetables don't read repo); ELB rarely binding in India
FRBM ceilings; crowding-out risk; political downward-rigidity of spending
Coordination
**Debt-management overlap** (RBI as government's banker) — the deficit-monetisation firewall (FRBM bar; WMA the liquidity valve); the growth-inflation assignment debate
Fiscal dominance risk when deficits force monetary accommodation — the independence question

sections.heading: Financial markets & development finance — the plumbing

items: **Market map**: money market (call, T-bills, CP-CD — the rate corridor's home), **G-sec market** (the risk-free curve), corporate bonds (shallow — RMI-006), equity (deep), forex (~$50+ bn/day), derivatives (exchange-traded giants) — regulated by **RBI (money-forex-G-sec), SEBI (securities), IRDAI-PFRDA** with **FSDC** as the coordination table.

**Development finance's arc**: DFI era (IDBI-ICICI-IFCI term-lending) → 1990s conversion to banks (the term-finance vacuum) → the **revival wave — NaBFID (2021, infra), NABARD (agri-rural), SIDBI (MSME), NHB (housing), EXIM, MUDRA** — plus market substitutes (InvITs, patient pools like NIIF ~$4-5 bn platform); the lesson: long-horizon lending needs institutions built for it, not converted from it.

**Reform frontier**: corporate-bond deepening (insolvency credibility + market-making), **GIFT-IFSC's** offshore-onshore bridge, digital-rupee (**e₹ pilots — wholesale & retail CBDC**), account-aggregator credit rails, and the climate-finance layer (sovereign green bonds ~₹20,000+ cr issues, RBI's climate-risk framework drafts).

**AP hook**: development finance touches the state as NABARD's RIDF (rural infra loans AP uses heavily), NaBFID-eligible port-energy projects, SIDBI's MSME clusters, and the SHG-bank linkage — the plumbing localised.

sections.heading: Investment in industry & infrastructure — the capex question

blocks.text: India's investment rate (~30-31% GFCF) must fund THREE simultaneous builds: **industrial capacity** (the manufacturing push), **infrastructure** (NIP's ₹111 lakh crore), and the **energy transition** (~$10+ trillion to 2070 estimates). The financing architecture: public capex (the post-2020 bridge — ~₹11 lakh crore union + states' window), private corporate capex (the awaited baton — capacity utilisation ~75%+ and deleveraged balance sheets set the stage), PPPs (HAM-TOT-VGF models), patient pools (NIIF, pension-insurance's infra allocations, InvITs ~₹5+ lakh crore AUM era), and external (FDI + multilateral + green finance).

rows: Land
The fixed factor: acquisition law (**RFCTLARR 2013** — consent 70-80%, compensation 2-4x), pooling alternatives (Amaravati), land banks (APIIC-model)
Land cost-certainty decides project math; digitised records (AP's resurvey) as investment infrastructure
Minerals & materials
Iron ore-bauxite-limestone adequacy; **critical-minerals dependence** (Li-Co-REE); cement-steel capacity as capex's own demand
MMDR auctions + criticals mission + recycling as the supply-side answer
**Energy**
The E2-013/016 base: coal plateau + RE surge + storage gap
Every industrial plan is an energy plan — power cost-reliability decides competitiveness (AP's firm-green pitch)
Water & logistics
Industrial water allocations (coastal advantage), ports-rail-road (Gati Shakti's synchronisation)
Coast + corridor = AP's structural pitch (IDA-044)

items: **Why private capex lagged a decade**: twin-balance-sheet hangover → demand uncertainty → 'why build when you can buy' (M&A cheaper than greenfield) → global shocks; the turn: deleveraging done, PLI's nudge, utilisation up — the cycle's turn visible in announcements if not yet fully in ground-breaking: state it with that honesty.

**Infrastructure's specific frictions**: land-clearance-litigation timelines, contract sanctity (the AP PPA lesson), DISCOM offtake risk in power, municipal capacity in urban infra — **de-risking (viability funds, credit enhancement, model concessions)** is the state's real job beyond money.

**The physical-resources strategy**: secure (criticals mission, coal-logistics), substitute (recycling, material efficiency), and site smartly (water-stressed vs coastal locations — the reason AP markets its coast) — resources as the capex plan's quiet constraint.

**AP synthesis**: the state IS the theme's case study — land banks + pooled capital city + ports + firm-green energy + resurveyed records: an investment-attraction stack built precisely on the physical-resources logic.
